title: Capacitors: Parallel-Plate Physics & Networks
theory: $Q = CV$; parallel plate $C = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 S}{d}$ ($S$ = plate area, Japanese notation); the field inside is uniform: $E = \dfrac{V}{d} = \dfrac{Q}{Cd}$. **Identify the constraint first**: a capacitor *disconnected* from its battery keeps $Q$ fixed; one *still connected* keeps $V$ fixed. In a DC circuit "after a sufficient time", capacitors carry no current — analyze by voltages. Combinations: **parallel adds C** (same $V$); **series adds reciprocals** (same $Q$ on each).
framework: Reduce the network from the outside in.
Push total charge/voltage back through the reduction tree (series branches share $Q$; parallel branches share $V$).

problems.title: Field inside an isolated charged capacitor

parts.parameters:
- Given: capacitance $C$, plate separation $d$, charge $Q$; battery disconnected.
- Find: electric field between the plates.
parts.conclusion: disconnection froze $Q$ — irrelevant here, decisive the moment plates move (then $E = Q/\varepsilon_0S$ is *separation-independent*). Units: $\mathrm{C/(F\cdot m)} = \mathrm{V/m}$ ✓.

problems.title: Charge on C₁ in a battery network

parts.parameters:
- Given: battery EMF $E$ with switch closed long ago; $C_1$ parallel $C_2$, that pair in series with $C_3$ across the battery.
- Find: charge stored on $C_1$.
parts.formulas: $C_{12} = C_1 + C_2$; series voltage division; $Q_1 = C_1V_{12}$.
parts.calculations: total $C = \dfrac{C_{12}C_3}{C_{12} + C_3}$; the series pair shares one charge, so $V_{12} = \dfrac{E\,C_3}{C_1 + C_2 + C_3}$; then $Q_1 = \dfrac{C_1C_3}{C_1 + C_2 + C_3}E$.
parts.conclusion: "after a sufficient period" = steady state, zero current, pure voltage bookkeeping. Limits: $C_3 \to \infty \Rightarrow V_{12} \to E,\ Q_1 \to C_1E$ ✓; $C_3 \to 0 \Rightarrow Q_1 \to 0$ ✓ — the two limits uniquely select (b).
